questions.question: A line graph shows how much water is in a rain barrel. On the vertical axis, each grid square stands for 5 cm. The point for Monday sits exactly 3 grid squares above the zero line. How much water was in the barrel on Monday?
options: 15 cm
5 cm
3 cm
8 cm
questions.explain: On a many-to-one scale you multiply: 3 squares × 5 cm each = 15 cm. The usual trap is counting squares instead of reading the scale, which gives the answer 3 cm.

questions.question: A line graph shows the money in Emma's savings jar at the end of each week. Week 1 is $4 and week 2 is $10, so the line climbs steeply. Week 4 is $30 and week 5 is $33, so the line climbs only gently. At the end of which week did Emma have the most money?
options: Week 2, because the line is steepest between week 1 and week 2
Week 5, because the point for week 5 is the highest, at $33
Week 4, because that is where the line stops going up quickly
Week 2, because the line climbs $6 there, more than the $3 climb later
questions.explain: How much money she has is shown by how HIGH the point is, so $33 in week 5 is the most. Steepness only tells you how fast the money changed, not how much she had.

questions.question: A line graph shows how many books a class read each month. On the vertical axis, each grid square stands for 10 books. The point for March sits exactly halfway between the 3rd and 4th grid lines above zero. How many books did the class read in March?
options: 3.5 books
30 books
35 books
40 books
questions.explain: The 3rd line is 30 books and the 4th is 40 books, so halfway is 35 books. Counting grid lines as if each were 1 book gives 3.5, which forgets that one square stands for 10.

questions.question: A line graph shows Liam's height on his birthday each year: 120 cm, then 126 cm, then 131 cm, then 135 cm. The line goes up every year, but each part of the line is a little less steep than the one before. What does the graph tell you about Liam?
options: He grew the same amount every year
He got shorter after year 2, because the line becomes less steep
He stopped growing after year 2, because the line flattens out
He grew taller every year, but grew a little less each year
questions.explain: The line keeps rising (120 → 126 → 131 → 135), so he keeps growing; the rises get smaller (6 cm, 5 cm, 4 cm), so the line gets less steep. A flatter line that still rises means slower growth, not shrinking or stopping.

questions.question: On a line graph, one grid square on the vertical axis stands for 4 units. The point for Tuesday is 6 squares above zero and the point for Wednesday is 9 squares above zero. How much did the value go up from Tuesday to Wednesday?
options: 12 units
3 units
36 units
9 units
questions.explain: Read both points first: 6 × 4 = 24 and 9 × 4 = 36, so the rise is 36 − 24 = 12 units. Subtracting the squares (9 − 6 = 3) forgets that each square counts for 4.

questions.question: Sofia and Noah each drew a line graph of their savings. On Sofia's graph one grid square stands for $2, and her line rises 3 squares from week 1 to week 2. On Noah's graph one grid square stands for $5, and his line rises 2 squares over the same two weeks. Whose savings grew more?
options: Sofia, because her line rises 3 squares and Noah's rises only 2
Noah, by $4
Sofia, because her line looks steeper on the page
They grew by the same amount
questions.explain: Always turn squares into real amounts before comparing: Sofia rose 3 × $2 = $6 and Noah rose 2 × $5 = $10, so Noah grew $4 more. Two graphs with different scales cannot be compared just by counting squares or by which line looks steeper.

questions.question: A line graph shows the water level in the school's fish tank through the day. Between 2 p.m. and 5 p.m. the line is flat (horizontal) at the 40 cm mark. What does that flat part of the line tell you?
options: Nobody measured the water between 2 p.m. and 5 p.m.
The water level dropped slowly during those hours
The water level stayed at 40 cm the whole time
The water level rose by 40 cm during those hours
questions.explain: A horizontal line means the value is not changing, so the level held at 40 cm from 2 p.m. to 5 p.m. A flat line is often mistaken for a slow drop, but slow dropping would still tilt downward.

questions.question: A line graph shows Maya's bean plant each week: week 1 is 8 cm, week 2 is 12 cm, week 3 is 20 cm, week 4 is 23 cm. Between which weeks did the plant grow the fastest, and how can you see it on the graph?
options: Weeks 3 to 4, because the line is highest there
Weeks 1 to 2, because that is where the line starts to climb
Every week is the same, because the line keeps going up
Weeks 2 to 3, because the line is steepest there, an 8 cm rise
questions.explain: Compare the rises: 4 cm, then 8 cm, then 3 cm, so weeks 2 to 3 is the biggest change and that is exactly the steepest part of the line. The highest point (23 cm in week 4) tells you the tallest the plant got, not where it grew fastest.

questions.question: A line graph shows how many passengers took the Horseshoe Bay ferry each day. Each grid square on the vertical axis stands for 50 passengers. Monday's point is 4 squares up, Tuesday's is 6 squares, Wednesday's is 3 squares and Thursday's is 7 squares. How many more passengers rode on the busiest day than on the quietest day?
options: 200 passengers
4 passengers
350 passengers
500 passengers
questions.explain: Busiest is Thursday, 7 × 50 = 350, and quietest is Wednesday, 3 × 50 = 150, so the difference is 350 − 150 = 200 passengers. Subtracting squares first (7 − 3 = 4) and forgetting the scale is the common slip.

questions.question: Ravi and Mei each drew a line graph of the SAME classroom temperature, which rose from 15 °C to 25 °C during the morning. On Ravi's graph each grid square stands for 1 °C, so his line rises 10 squares. On Mei's graph each grid square stands for 5 °C, so her line rises 2 squares. Ravi's line looks much steeper. Which statement is true?
options: Ravi's graph shows a bigger rise, because his line is steeper
Both graphs show the same 10 °C rise; Ravi's line only looks steeper because his scale is stretched out
Mei's graph shows a bigger rise, because each of her squares counts for 5 °C
Ravi's rise of 10 squares is 5 times Mei's rise of 2 squares, so his rise is 5 times bigger
questions.explain: Both lines show 25 − 15 = 10 °C, since 10 × 1 = 10 and 2 × 5 = 10. Steepness depends on the scale you choose, so you must read the scale before you trust how steep a line looks.

questions.question: Jayden graphs the rain collected in the class rain gauge. Each grid square stands for 6 mm. His points are week 1 at 12 mm, week 2 at 18 mm, week 3 at 24 mm and week 4 at 30 mm, and the line rises by exactly one square each week. If the pattern keeps going, what should the point for week 5 be?
options: 31 mm, because the line goes up a little each week
5 mm, because the next point would be 5 squares above zero
36 mm, because the line rises one square, or 6 mm, each week
60 mm, because the line has been rising steeply
questions.explain: First find the trend from the graph: each week the line climbs one square, and one square is 6 mm, so 30 + 6 = 36 mm. Reading the next point as 5 squares = '5 mm' ignores the many-to-one scale.
